div.l: And with wᵒrthi wrthi worthi wemen of the toun
For he hadde power of confessioun
As seide hȳm self more than a curat
For of hese ordere he was licencyat
Ful swetli herde he confessioun
And plesaunt was hese absolucyoun
He was an esi man to ȝeue penaıı̄unce
There as he wiste to han a good petauns
Vnto pore orderis for to ȝeue
Is ygne that a man Iˢ I Is wel I schreue
For ȝif he ȝaf he durste make auaunt
He wiste that a man was repentaunt
For manye a man so hard is of hese herte
He may not wepe though hȳm sore smerte
Therfore in stede of wepyng ⁊and preyeres
Men mote ȝeue silủer to the pore freres
¶ Hise tipet was ay farsed ful of knyuys
And pynnys for to ȝeuyn fayre wywes
And serteynli he hadde a merye throte
Wel couthe he synge ⁊and pleyen on a rote
Of ȝeddyngis he bar vttyrli the prys
His nekke whit was as the flour delis
Therto he strong was as a chaumpioıı̄un
He knew the tauernys wel in euery toun
And eueryche osteler ⁊and tapstere
Bet than a laser or a bakystere
For vn to swich a worthi man as he
Acordith not as by his faculte
To haue with swiche sike men a queyntaıı̄unce
It is not honest it may not auauce
For to dele with non swich parayle
But al with riche ⁊and selleris of vitayle
And oủeral there profit schulde aryse
Curteys he was ⁊and louly of seruyse
Ther was no man now so v̉ertywous
NHNe was the beste beᵍgere begere beggere in hese hous
